etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English byldynge, buyldyng, byldyng, buldynge, buldyng, boldyng, equivalent to build +‎ -ing. Compare also related Middle English bold (“edifice, castle, mansion”), from Old English bold (“building, dwelling, house”).

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The act or process by which something is built; construction.
(countable) A closed structure with walls and a roof.

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Mark Tran, “Denied an education by war”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 1:
quote.text: One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools […] as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks.

quote.citation: 2024 May 6, @thepunbible, Twitter‎[1], archived from the original on 28 June 2024:
quote.text: Why doesn't Italy finish their buildings

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English beeldynge, equivalent to build +‎ -ing.

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of build
